subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should this PR remove system-tag defanging in favor of provenance-marked inbound context and downstream system-event rendering, accepting Doctor-owned upgrade repair for persisted state?
rationale: This is an intentional security and compatibility boundary change rather than a narrow mechanical defect; the repository member and protected labels require a maintainer to choose the permanent trust-model direction.

options.title: Require complete boundary audit
options.body: Keep the refactor direction, but require focused evidence that every queue, gateway, hook, and transcript presentation path cannot emit forged trusted-looking system lines before merge.

options.title: Retain boundary sanitization
options.body: Keep the plain-label and marker work while preserving narrowly scoped sanitization at external system-event ingestion points.

options.title: Pause the refactor
options.body: Defer the label and sanitizer redesign until a maintainer-owned trust-boundary design is agreed for all prompt and event surfaces.

recommendation.title: Require complete boundary audit
recommendation.body: Keep the refactor direction, but require focused evidence that every queue, gateway, hook, and transcript presentation path cannot emit forged trusted-looking system lines before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is the only concretely identified repository member connected to the current branch and can supply the requested implementation evidence; final policy approval remains with the relevant security/maintainer reviewers.
